name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Ed Case running with solid fundraising
Republican challenger Adriel Lam with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Case: a D+13 district, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge over a little-known challenger, with markets also pricing a near-certain Democratic win. With no polls or expert ratings available, uncertainty stays elevated but the race remains safely Democratic.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually favorable national environment for Republicans could narrow the expected margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's 1st District is a solidly Democratic seat, and incumbent Ed Case is seeking another term after renomination. He has raised about $1.1 million and holds roughly $600,000 on hand, while Republican Adriel Lam reports no fundraising figures. Minor-party candidates are on the ballot but lack visible resources.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's D+13 lean, Case's incumbency and financial advantage, and prediction markets that price a Democratic win around 95 percent. The expected margin is roughly 22 points, keeping the seat in the Safe Democratic column with moderate confidence.
